subject: LLM request routing, processing locations and cross-border transfer logistics — Healthly Q&A
summary: Prospect asked for explicit details on where LLM inference requests are executed, which subprocessors touch payloads, and how cross-border transfers and deletion SLAs work. Thread covers regional execution, transient caching behavior, subprocessors, and next steps for DPA/technical evidence.
messages:
From: Sana Rao <sana@healthly.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: where our requests are processed + transfer picture

Hi Jordan,

Quick one as we prep our security review: can you confirm where Redwood executes inference for hosted requests from our EU users? We need a concise list of regions that might process request payloads, which subprocessors (cloud, telemetry, KMS) could touch data, and whether any cross-border transfers to the US (or elsewhere) happen by default. Also: are there options to pin execution to an EU-only footprint or to use a private deployment?

If you can send a short bullet list plus any simple diagram or CSV of subprocessors, that would be ideal — we’ll attach to our procurement ticket.

Thanks,
Sana Rao
Security & Privacy, Healthly
---
Healthly | sana@healthly.ai | +44 20 7946 08xx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sana Rao <sana@healthly.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: where our requests are processed + transfer picture

Hi Sana — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front then a few attachments for evidence: redwood-residency-factsheet-2027-10.pdf and transfer-topology-diagram-2027-10.png are attached, plus a CSV with our subprocessor roster.

High-level bullets:
- Regions where inference may execute (hosted): EU (Frankfurt, Dublin), US (us-west-2, us-central-1), APAC (Singapore) depending on routing and customer-configured preference.
- Default hosted behavior: requests are routed to the lowest-latency compatible model endpoint. For EU accounts we can enable region pinning to keep execution in EU regions only (model availability constraints apply).
- Subprocessors that may touch payloads: cloud compute providers (AWS, GCP, Azure depending on region), telemetry & observability partners for metrics collection (TelemetryOps — logs are sampled and redacted by default), and our KMS/HSM provider for key management (KeySafe). Full CSV attached.
- Cross-border transfers: by default, hosted requests may traverse or land in non-EU regions unless EU pinning is enabled. When EU pinning is requested we run inference only in EU regions and we can configure egress restrictions for associated logs/telemetry.
- Caching and transient storage: runtime-level prefix/KV caches are transient and configurable; in hosted mode default cache sojourn is short-lived (2 hours) and is not used for long-term storage. Persistent telemetry and audit logs follow the retention in the DPA.

Technical / contract next steps: looping in Marissa for the execution topology and Monica for deletion/DPA questions. If you can share a minimal list of controls you need in your procurement ticket (e.g., EU-only execution, 30/90/365-day log retention, KMS key ownership), we’ll map to options.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions (Redwood Inference)
Mobile: +1 415 555 01xx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sana Rao <sana@healthly.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: where our requests are processed + transfer picture — technical detail

Hi Sana — thanks for the question. I’m Marissa (runtime product) — a few technical clarifications to help your infra and security teams evaluate.

1) Execution footprint details- Hosted endpoints: we maintain model runtime pools in the regions listed above. Each request is routed by policy: latency-first by default; customers may elect region-pin policies at the org or route level (EU-only pinning supported for verified models).- Dedicated/Private: for customers on Dedicated or Private we can lock execution to customer-dedicated pools inside a VPC/region you pick (on-prem also available with our Private bundle).

2) Subprocessor behavior (who sees what)- Compute providers (AWS/GCP/Azure): handle encrypted request payloads on the VMs/GPUs; Redwood manages the runtime and keying.- TelemetryOps (observability): receives aggregated metrics and sampled traces. Sensitive fields are redacted at ingest per our redaction rules; full request payloads are not forwarded to third-party telemetry by default.- KeySafe (KMS/HSM): stores root keys; data encryption keys used for storage and any customer-managed keys are provisioned via KMS APIs.

3) Transient caches & logs- KV/prefix caches: used to accelerate repeated prefixes; default TTL is 2 hours in hosted. You can opt-out or set TTL=0 for privacy-sensitive routes.- Request logs: ephemeral execution traces (request id, model, latency) are retained for 30 days by default; full audit logs (for billing/troubleshooting) retention is configurable via the Console (30/90/365). We can offer reduced retention for procurement/regulatory needs.

4) Cross-border transfers & legal safeguards- When EU pinning is enabled no request bodies are routed outside EU execution pools. However, certain operational traces or failover substitutions may trigger cross-region routing in extreme cases; these are audited.- Contracts & transfer mechanisms: we use SCCs for EU->US transfers where applicable and offer a DPA with data transfer clauses. Private deployments avoid cross-border transfers entirely.

5) Evidence we can provide- Transfer topology diagram (attached)
- Subprocessor inventory CSV (attached)
- SOC 2 report and encryption architecture diagram (available on request / under NDA)

If you want I can prepare a short table mapping your control requirements to exact config knobs (e.g., pinning + TTL + KMS ownership). Let me know which controls are must-haves.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product — Runtime (Redwood Inference)
From: Sana Rao <sana@healthly.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2027 10:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: where our requests are processed + transfer picture — follow-ups

Thanks Jordan / Marissa — super helpful. Couple follow-ups so we can close our procurement item: 

1) Deletion behavior: if we request per-request payload deletion (for example, delete all payloads for a given request id), what timelines do you commit to for hosted vs dedicated vs private?
2) Embeddings/vectors: do embeddings derived from customer data count as customer data for deletion/retention? If we ask for deletion, are vectors purged from caches and long-term stores?
3) Audit visibility: will we be able to see an audit trail confirming a deletion action (request id, timestamp, operator) in the Console or via API?

We’ll likely want EU pinning + customer-managed KMS if possible. Also please send the DPA/DocuSign link when ready.

Appreciate it,
Sana
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sana Rao <sana@healthly.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: where our requests are processed + transfer picture — deletions & next steps

Hi Sana — Monica here (contracts & security ops). Answers and next steps below.

Deletion timelines- Hosted: for standard hosted accounts we commit to logical deletion of request payloads from hot runtime caches within 6 hours and to purge request bodies from persistent internal stores within 30 days after a verified deletion request.- Dedicated: Dedicated customers can request accelerated purge policies; typical contract language supports purge from persistent stores within 7 days.- Private (VPC/on-prem): deletion is under customer control — we provide the tooling and scripts; timeline depends on your hosting environment.

Embeddings and derived artifacts- Vectors/embeddings produced from customer payloads are treated as customer data. If you request deletion we will purge embeddings from long-term stores and indices as part of the deletion workflow. Note: short-lived caches (TTL default 2 hours) may contain derived tokens; those are cleared by the runtime purge. For large embedding indexes there is an asynchronous removal process; we provide an audit of removed object ids.

Audit trail & verification- Console + API: deletion requests generate an auditable operation id; the Console shows status and timestamp, and our API returns operation_id, initiated_by, and completion_timestamp. We can also provide signed attestation for deletion events on request (SLA/fee may apply).

Contract & DPA- DPA: https://docusign.com/MLL-DPA-Healthly-2027 (linked) — this includes data transfer clauses and options for customer-managed KMS.

Next steps- I’ll drop a short configuration template (EU-pin: true, KMS: customer-managed, retention: 30 days logs) and a one-page mapping of controls to config flags. Jordan will coordinate a quick tech call if your infra team wants to validate the transfer topology.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Head of Enterprise Contracts — Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 650 555 02xx
